clue.text: Between us, it's how to get things taped

definitions.meaning: said in confidence, not for publication or quotation
read literally, a recording made by copying from a disc

explanation.surface: Someone explains confidentiality while musing on how to make recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark kept confidential is not for publishing, and a tape copied from a vinyl disc is taken literally from the platter.

clue.text: Manage to define the bishop's position

definitions.meaning: to supervise or direct
a bishop's role is to supervise a diocese; also, read as two words, position above a see

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to sort out what exactly a bishop's job is.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to manage, and supervising the flock of a diocese is the defining duty of a bishop.

clue.text: Wealthy patrons of large old technology colleges

parts.note: fat means large or plump
CATs were Colleges of Advanced Technology, a former kind of British institution later turned into universities

explanation.surface: Rich benefactors are thanked for funding former technical colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: CATs, Colleges of Advanced Technology, were British higher-education colleges of the 1950s and 60s, most of which became universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich and privileged people, especially donors with influence, are called this in idiomatic slang.

clue.text: An uncompromising advocate ofthe iron steamship

parts.note: iron as an adjective means hard, as in an iron will
a liner is a large passenger steamship

explanation.surface: A diehard supporter of an ironclad ocean vessel is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'ofthe' is the newspaper's run-together 'of the', a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks rigidly to a policy and refuses compromise is a rigid advocate in political idiom.

clue.text: Schemes which Rex takes advantage of

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king
to use someone is to exploit or take advantage of them

explanation.surface: A man named Rex is accused of exploiting other people's plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricks or stratagems meant to deceive are schemes.

clue.text: Interior decor in the Greek city

indicators.note: the inside of the words decor in the holds the letters wanted, with the outer letters dropped

explanation.surface: Someone admires the interior design of a home in an ancient Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient city-state on the isthmus between mainland Greece and the Peloponnese, still a modern town.

clue.text: Ronald takes some water in France while writing a poem

parts.note: Ron is the short form of the name Ronald
French for some water is de l'eau, loosely given here as de eau

explanation.surface: A man named Ronald sips water on a French holiday while composing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some water in France' renders the French phrase for some water as DE EAU, skipping the elision.
explanation.definitionFit: A short French verse form with a refrain and only two rhymes, a type of poem.

clue.text: Depressed because the hard stuff's running out

definitions.meaning: feeling gloomy or downcast
taken literally, a short supply of strong liquor

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy because the whisky bottle is nearly empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gloomy is an idiom for dejection, and literally having little strong liquor left in the house.

clue.text: Rarely the hotel in which to find a single celebrity

definitions.text: Rarely the hotel in which to find a single celebrity

parts.note: one means single
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A basic budget hotel is seldom where famous people stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic hotel with the lowest rating seldom attracts famous guests, while the pieces are a lone famous person.

clue.text: Recoils from describing psychiatrists in vulgar terms

definitions.meaning: draws back in fear or distaste
a slang name for psychiatrists, from headshrinker

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at hearing mental-health doctors called rude names.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch away is to draw back, and head doctors are known by a slangy name from headhunting tribes.

clue.text: Ways to diet on a limited budget?

definitions.meaning: taken literally, methods of becoming thin
living on small income, little money

explanation.surface: A question suggests that slimming plans suit someone who has little money.
explanation.definitionFit: Methods of getting thin, read literally, and an idiom for a small income.

clue.text: Place whither the Magi bore their offerings

definitions.meaning: to set or put in position

definitions.text: whither the Magi bore their offerings
definitions.meaning: the wise men brought gifts to the infant Jesus lying in a manger in a stable, read as two words

explanation.surface: A nativity scene: the Wise Men bring gifts to a particular spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something in position is to put it in, and the wise men went into the stable stall of Bethlehem.

clue.text: Frank from then on has taken note

parts.note: since means from that time onwards
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A man named Frank has written a note ever since that day.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest and candid, without pretence, as a straightforward person is.

clue.text: Appears to view a manuscript

parts.note: to see is to view

explanation.surface: Someone shows up to look at an old handwritten document.
explanation.definitionFit: To look or give the impression is to come across a certain way.

clue.text: The dogged reporter

parts.note: dogged suggests tenacious, but also hints at a hunting dog that sniffs out stories

explanation.surface: A persistent journalist chases a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenacious journalist who hunts out stories is called by a canine nickname.

clue.text: A mad shot in the dark

definitions.text: A mad shot in the dark

parts.words: A mad shot in the dark
parts.note: a reckless attempt made without any information, a random stab at an answer

explanation.surface: Someone fires a crazy round into the night.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfounded conjecture made at random is a reckless stab.

clue.text: By and large, where ultimate military authority lies

definitions.meaning: on the whole, usually
read as two words, power rests with a senior officer of the top rank

explanation.surface: A remark that, broadly speaking, top army officers hold all power.
explanation.definitionFit: On the whole means mostly, and read literally the top officer holds command.

clue.text: The old minstrel is a merry fellow

definitions.meaning: a medieval travelling singer or musician
read as two words, a man full of mirth

explanation.surface: A minstrel of times past is described as a jolly chap.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a medieval singer, and read literally a man of joy.

clue.text: He's crackers, and needs crackers to crack it

definitions.meaning: describes a person who is mad; the answer names such a person
read literally, a shell of a nut which requires nutcrackers to open

explanation.surface: A madman is said to need a nutcracker to deal with his problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for a lunatic, and read literally the hard shell around a kernel.

clue.text: Just take in an apprentice showing talent

indicators.note: the word for just takes in, or encloses, the letter for a learner

parts.note: fair means just or even-handed
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Simply hire a trainee who shows real ability.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude or gift for something is a knack or talent.

clue.text: Cunning strategy to impose financial deterrents on the Home Counties

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties that deter wrongdoing
the counties around London, in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A plan to levy penalties on the wealthy area around London is called clever.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in the South East (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle skill or an artful manoeuvre is delicate cunning, also a bridge stratagem.

clue.text: Insect consuming citrus fruit for nourishment

indicators.note: the insect eats, so swallows and holds, the citrus fruit inside it

parts.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A bug eats a lime as food.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or sustenance is a rather formal word for nourishment.

clue.text: Imagined getting one date arranged with newspaper boss

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the letters of date are rearranged

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone fantasised about fixing a date with the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceive or form a thought of something is to picture it in the mind.

clue.text: The laundry Eric patronises certainly contains one

indicators.note: the words laundry Eric hold within them the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A laundrette that Eric uses surely has a tumble machine.
explanation.definitionFit: 'One' stands for the item a laundrette is sure to hold, a machine for drying clothes.

clue.text: The man going to a French island is not a Jew

parts.note: a gent is a man
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A man setting out for an island off France is identified by religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is not Jewish is called this, from the Latin for of a nation.

clue.text: Instant run-down

definitions.meaning: immediate, done without delay or formality
a brief account of the main points

explanation.surface: A quick overview of the main points.
explanation.definitionFit: Summary justice is instant, and a recap or synopsis is a run-down of the main points.

clue.text: Oriental of earnest disposition

indicators.note: disposition as an arrangement means the letters of earnest are set out anew

explanation.surface: Someone from the Orient is said to be of a serious temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging the letters of 'earnest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from or relating to the Orient means belonging to Asia.

clue.text: With hindsight, interceptors needed to be dispersed

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of interceptors are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Looking back, the fighter planes ought to have been spread out.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking back on past events, with the benefit of later knowledge.
